key_insight: Embodied manipulation needs a structured data strategy, not just more data. This paper proposes a five-level "data pyramid" that ranks embodied data sources by how directly they connect observations, physical state, and actions.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a unified way to organize and compare data sources for embodied agents. Unlike web-scale language/vision models, embodied systems need data tied to real physical interactions, which comes from many fragmented sources with different levels of realism and supervision.
method: Organize embodied data into a pyramid of five complementary sources: real-robot data, UMI-style data, egocentric/exocentric data, simulation data, and general vision-language data.
Use the pyramid to show how each source contributes different strengths, from high-fidelity action grounding to broad visual-language coverage.
Provide a framework for thinking about data collection and model training across the embodied AI ecosystem.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this gives a practical roadmap for choosing and combining datasets when training embodied agents. It helps balance realism, scale, and cost, making it easier to design more capable manipulation systems.
visual_elements: A pyramid diagram with five labeled tiers from base to top
Icons for each data source: robot arm, wearable camera, scene cameras, simulator, internet-scale model
A comparison table showing fidelity, cost, scale, and action grounding for each tier
A flow graphic linking data sources to embodied manipulation capabilities
paper_authors: Yifan Ye, Yankai Fu, Yaoxu Lv, Bohan Hou, Jun Cen
